title: Cap. IV Arg. 1: gospel-revealed will to save perseverers is the whole predestination decree
pass_a_gloss: Argument 1. The will of God concerning the salvation and ruin of men revealed in the Gospel is the whole entire decree of predestination: To will to save those persevering in faith, but to will to leave wrath upon the unbelieving and impenitent, is the will of God concerning the salvation and ruin of men revealed in the Gospel: Therefore to will to save those persevering in faith, but to leave wrath upon the unbelieving, is the whole and entire decree of predestination. They say the major is manifest of itself, and does not need proof; the minor expressly founded in these places of Scripture, John 3:36, Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; but whoever does not obey the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him. And John 6:40, This is the will of him who sent me, that whoever sees the Son, and believes in him, may have eternal life.
pass_b_english: Arg. 1. God's will concerning men's salvation and ruin, revealed in the Gospel, is the whole entire decree of predestination. To will to save those persevering in faith, and to leave wrath on the unbelieving and impenitent, is that gospel-revealed will. Therefore to will to save perseverers in faith and leave wrath on unbelievers is the whole and entire decree of predestination. They say the major is self-evident and needs no proof; the minor is expressly founded in John 3:36 — Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; whoever does not obey the Son will not see life, but God's wrath remains on him — and John 6:40 — This is the will of him who sent me, that whoever sees the Son and believes in him may have eternal life.
source_text: Arg. 1. Voluntas Dei de salute et exitio hominum in Evangelio patefacta, est totum integrum decretum praedestinationis: Perseverantes in fide velle servare, iram vero super incredulis et impoenitentibus velle relinquere, est voluntas Dei de salute et exitio hominum in Evangelio patefacta: Ergo perseverantes in fide velle servare, iram vero super incredulis relinquere, est totum et integrum decretum praedestinationis. Majorem dicunt esse per se manifestam, nec probatione indigere; Minorem in hisce Scripturae locis expresse fundatam Joh. iii. 36, Qui credit in Filium, habet vitam aeternam; qui vero Filio non obtemperat, non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super ipsum. Et Joh. vi. 40, Haec est voluntas ejus qui misit me, ut quisquis videt Filium, et credit in eum, habeat vitam aeternam.
